territorial_scope.description: Applies to AI-generated or simulated voice calls subject to the US Telephone Consumer Protection Act and the Commission's implementing rules.

evidence.quote: encompass current AI technologies that resemble human voices

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: FCC declaratory ruling applying the TCPA's restrictions on artificial or prerecorded voice calls to AI technologies that generate or simulate human voices, including voice cloning. Callers need prior express consent absent an emergency purpose or exemption, and must give caller identification and disclosure. Effective upon release, 8 February 2024.
summary.long: Declaratory ruling of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC 24-17, CG Docket No. 23-362), adopted 2 February 2024 and released 8 February 2024. It confirms that the Telephone Consumer Protection Act's restrictions on calls using an 'artificial or prerecorded voice' cover current AI technologies that resemble human voices or generate call content using a prerecorded voice, including voice cloning (paras. 1-5). Under the ruling, callers using such technologies must obtain the called party's prior express consent before initiating the call, absent an emergency purpose or exemption, and the presence of a live agent on the call does not change this (paras. 5, 8-9). Calls must state the identity of the entity responsible for initiating them, and advertising or telemarketing calls must offer specified opt-out methods, under existing 47 CFR 64.1200(b) rules (para. 9). The ruling is effective upon release (para. 11) and follows a November 2023 Notice of Inquiry (paras. 4, 8). The ruling itself sets no penalties. The separate commissioner statements refer to enforcement by State Attorneys General and the FCC's authority, but those statements are not operative provisions.

notes: Declaratory ruling (FCC 24-17, CG Docket No. 23-362), adopted 2024-02-02 and released 2024-02-08; effective upon release (para. 11). Operative text is paras. 1-11; the three commissioner statements are not operative and are used for context only. Internal points: footnote 4 gives the cite as CFR § 64.1200(a)(3), (9) without the title number; footnote 13 says prior express written consent is required for advertisement or telemarketing calls, while paras. 2 and 5 refer to prior express consent generally. The operative text states no penalty amounts. Relation target IDs are blank because no registry IDs were supplied.

entities.note: The operative text names no firm or facility and designates no public body. The Commission issues the ruling; State Attorneys General, the FTC and the FEC appear only in separate statements or footnotes.

thresholds.note: The declaratory ruling interprets the TCPA's restriction on artificial or prerecorded voice calls and sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Numbers in the text (e.g., number of State Attorneys General, forfeiture amount in a cited order) are not thresholds.

enforcement.note: The declaratory ruling creates no sanction regime and states no penalty, fine or damages amount. It restates that calls using AI-generated or prerecorded voices need prior express consent under 47 U.S.C. § 227(b) and 47 CFR § 64.1200 (paras. 2, 5, 9), and those provisions are cited, not reproduced. Commissioner statements mention a State AG damages route and a prior FCC forfeiture (Rosenworcel statement; Starks statement n.2), but these are non-operative and were not coded as enforcement.
